newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money market rates stable in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money market rates stable in slow trade.

text.p: Croatian money market rates were stable in slow morning trade, but demand has not been fully met despite abundant supply as some banks could not agree on terms.
"Trading was pretty difficult today," dealer Jasenka Blagaic told Reuters. "Reported demand was quite substantial, but some creditors could not agree on terms with borrowers."
She said some creditors had stricter criteria, while others abstained awaiting bigger cash outflaw next week.
Morning settlements totalled 16.1 million kuna, but 10 million kuna in demand found no creditors leaving 22 million surplus on the supply side.
Three quarters accounted for call-money deals at the usual 10.5 percent rate and one smaller transaction was made at 26 percent.
Term one-month loans were granted at 14 and 15 percent.
Overnight trade on Thursday was modest at 12 million kuna, sought by two banks with shortfalls and one savings bank maintaining its mandatory reserves.
